summary: The note previews the Local Business Fair, held September 15th to 17th, 2023, which supports home-grown entrepreneurs facing competition from online giants and large retailers. It covers networking, seminars and workshops, access to capital, technology help, consumer awareness and guidance on bureaucracy and scaling. Local entrepreneurs' stories illustrate both the struggles and the opportunities the fair provides.
one_line: The Local Business Fair (Sept 15-17, 2023) offers networking, workshops, funding access and bureaucratic help to support struggling local entrepreneurs.
key_facts: The Local Business Fair is set to take place from September 15th to 17th, 2023.
Sarah Johnson owns the handcrafted soap boutique 'Bubble Dreams' and says she battles online giants and one-click purchases made at 2 AM.
Steve Anderson, founder of the electronics repair shop 'TechTonics', says last year's Business Fair connected him with suppliers and like-minded entrepreneurs, calling it 'a lifeline'.
Networking at the fair can lead to collaborations, bulk purchasing to drive down costs, and shared marketing campaigns.
Seminar topics include 'Digital Marketing on a Shoestring Budget,' 'Navigating Small Business Taxes,' and 'Crafting an Unforgettable Brand Identity'.
Business mentor Victoria Lee will lead a roundtable titled 'Innovation in Isolation: Cultivating a Competitive Edge'.
The fair invites local credit unions, community banks and potential investors to meet entrepreneurs face-to-face, since banks often favor established companies.
Manuel Ortiz's eco-friendly packaging initiative was funded through a crowdfunded campaign after last year's fair.
The 'Tech Advancements for Small Businesses' section covers point-of-sale systems and customer relationship management software for those with limited budgets.
Joan Meyers, an advocate for sustainable shopping, will chair the workshop 'Your Money, Your Community: The Power of Local Purchases'.
Representatives from local government offices will help entrepreneurs with regulatory hurdles, zoning issues and licensing.
Panel discussions will feature entrepreneurs who have successfully scaled from home-office businesses to community industry staples.
